brief: Stronger-than-expected August jobs data and more hawkish Fed commentary lead UBS to now expect two 25bp Fed hikes in 2026, in September and December, taking the fed funds range to 4.00-4.25%. Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August versus a consensus estimate of 55,000. Because a hiking path is now expected, UBS raised its Treasury yield forecasts: 2-year yields to 4.25% by June 2027, 100bps higher than its previous forecast, and 10-year yields to 4.5%, 40bps higher than its prior forecast. The hiking path also means the relative advantage of short-duration quality bonds over cash should narrow, so UBS no longer thinks quality bonds will beat cash. Short-duration bonds can still offer attractive income, but capital-gain potential is more limited and further upward repricing of the policy path could weigh on returns. As a result, UBS sees opportunities to diversify portfolio income: selective exposure to higher-yielding, growth-sensitive segments such as emerging-market credit, high yield, and subordinated debt, while avoiding overexposure to any single credit segment, plus equity income, structured income strategies, and multi-asset approaches. UBS estimates a multi-asset income portfolio investing internationally and dynamically across cash, bonds, equities, and derivatives could offer roughly 5-7% annual income.
